frequency_question: How often do major structural reform bills successfully clear all legislative veto points and pass into law within a short calendar window?
membership_rule: Includes major bipartisan energy, infrastructure, or regulatory reform packages proposed in Congress since 1995. Excluded are routine appropriations, must-pass defense authorization bills (NDAA), and purely partisan reconciliation bills that bypassed regular order.

cases.name: Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007
American Clean Energy and Security Act (Waxman-Markey)
Energy Permitting Reform Act attempts (Manchin bill)

coverage_note: 5 major documented attempts at comprehensive energy reform/permitting overhaul since 1995; 3 resulted in major signed legislation, 2 stalled.
known_gaps: Minor rider provisions attached to must-pass omnibus spending bills are excluded, focusing solely on standalone or primary omnibus energy/permitting reform attempts.
skeleton: Legislative sessions since 1995 where comprehensive energy/infrastructure reform was actively negotiated under divided or narrow-majority control, multiplied by the fraction resulting in enacted statute.
multiplier: 5 major legislative push cycles evaluated; 3 enacted successfully, 2 failed.
validity_reason: Legislative polarization structures and committee veto gate dynamics change slowly over multi-decade congressional eras.
